version: Complete Level 3 path v18: evidence-led second test, comparison after two observations, optional cancellable third and modal spotlight guide

notes: Before this revision, the previous v17 source and downloads were archived on GitHub at archive/pre-level3-path-v17, commit 5d56d4cbb763b039b4a8a7a4c3bceb7932f303b2. Earlier archives, numbered downloads and validation reports remain unchanged.

The complete player path now uses a free first allocation and an evidence-led second allocation. After two observed tests, the player can compare both actual results and continue directly to Alex’s response. Test another idea opens an optional third; Back to comparison discards unsubmitted edits and preserves the two recorded results. Reopening starts from the last tested allocation with unconfirmed controls. There is no fourth test.

Abstract aim radios, preselected strategies, numerical examples, automatically set suggested weights, compulsory contrast patterns, the required third test and the final keep/rethink gate have been removed. Optional Need a hint? provides only verbal scaffolding. Exact repeats remain invalid, while changed allocations with unchanged effort bands remain valid evidence.

Each later editor shows a compact Last observation grouped by the actual selected metric names and effort bands. Its short question follows the previous observation, including first-even, uneven all-covered, low-attention and unchanged-band histories. First-even attention is acknowledged rather than treated as a numerical failure; scoring-directed stopping remains a separate observation across allocations.

The guide is now a once-per-visit native modal spotlight with static Next/Back/Skip/Escape and a final Try your weights action. It highlights the actual slider, Confirm, remaining pair and Run. It changes no allocation and requires no practice. Keyboard focus, responsive bounds and reopening the guide with the optional Back control are browser checked.

Retained v17 rules are checked across all 4,851 legal positive integer splits: each weight 1–98, total 100, independent minimum 1–24 / steady 25–66 / intense 67–98 bands and monotone own-share effort. Near-even is descriptive max-minus-min ≤ 10 points, never an effort override. Linked-pair confirmation, either-order adjustment, positive native bounds, locked values and snapshot copies remain.

The comparison contains the actual two or three trial records. Every later cell labels More/Less/Same effort relative to the preceding trial by metric identity; quiet percentage references do not imply proportional effort. Actual unchanged patterns receive matching concluding dialogue rather than a false shift claim. Repeated effort-summary boxes, per-column aim headings and extra verdict controls are absent.

Seven pure suites pass 33 checks, including 13,200 complete cross-level dialogue paths, 320 two/three-test dialogue histories, legacy intent independence and 24 distinct emoji. Browser checks cover first-even and uneven starts, same-band results, partial completion ticks, optional-third cancellation, scene replay, timing visibility, exact-repeat recovery and 320/390/768/1366 px layouts. Imported pure modules were unchanged by the final workbench-only cancel/spotlight fixes; final-build browser tests cover both.

Partner-host checks verify dynamic opening names, distinct portraits, Level 2’s original selected trio inherited and editable, stable scene IDs, actual immutable run payloads, once-only completion after two or three tests, no newly populated intent/decision fields, nullable compared pairs and custom renderer replacement. The endpoint remains theory.reveal; no Design Lab navigation occurs.

All four builds and all five latest ZIPs pass. CRC/SHA256 and byte comparisons establish that packages match the final builds and manifest. Actual standalone Level 1/2/3 downloads and the connected Level 1 → 2 → 3 game are exercised offline. The review ZIP contains both standalone Level 3 and connected Levels 1–3 from those same builds.

This completes the approved Level 3 path revision, preserving Level 1/2 gameplay and the partner’s authored animation scripts. Opening integration and the separately requested Level 2 growth framing remain outside this step. Functional checks do not establish the best possible learning design, measured learning efficacy, classroom capacity or direct-file compatibility in every user browser.
